name: relay runtime two fix pilot
prompt:
Fix both defects in this TypeScript service runtime. Preserve the exported interfaces and make changes only to existing src/*.ts files. Do not inspect evaluator files or change the task requirements. Use the assigned retrieval provider and the controlled read, edit and test actions; you have at most 16 total actions and 3 test actions. There are no network or third party runtime dependencies.

Task 1: Make TTLCache a correct bounded LRU cache. An entry is expired at now >= expiresAt. Expired entries must not count toward size or cause a live entry to be evicted. get on a live entry refreshes its recency. set on an existing key replaces its value, refreshes expiration from the current time and makes it most recent without consuming another capacity slot. If live capacity is exceeded, evict the least recently used live key. A zero TTL removes the key. Keep the existing capacity and TTL validation.

Task 2: Correct retry's attempt and deadline bounds. maxAttempts includes the initial operation call, and attempt numbers begin at one. Do not call sleep after the final permitted failed attempt or when the deadline has already been reached. No operation may start at or after the absolute deadlineMs. Before a retry, clip the fixed delay to the remaining deadline time, then recheck the deadline after waiting. If the deadline is already reached before any attempt, reject with RetryDeadlineError. Once an operation has failed, exhausting either bound must reject with that exact most recent failure value. A successful operation that began before the deadline is accepted even if it completes after the deadline. Keep existing option validation.

Use the controlled test action to verify both fixes. Report what changed and any remaining failures. This is an exploratory pilot; do not claim comparative superiority.

cache: update refreshes TTL and LRU order without extra capacity
retry: no wait after final attempt or reached deadline
late completion of timely successful attempt accepted

limitations: Two authored tasks bundled into one session. Deterministic hidden tests measure these requirements, not general agent ability or all product capabilities. No provider results exist at fixture creation.
